text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Swedish public sector white collar workers worry more about losing their jobs than their colleagues in other countries, an OECD report showed. Only 15 percent of the workers are certain that they will be able to keep their jobs.
- The Swedish central bank's inflation target of two percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side could be too low, new research from the U.S. shows.
The study says an optimal inflation level is just below three percent and that inflation of up to five percent gives positive net effects.
- Ludmila Engquist, a Russian-born high hurdler, took Sweden's first medal in the world games in Athens when winning the 100m hurdles final on Sunday, the last day of the games.

- Sixteen countries, led by Sweden, call for fellow United Nations members not to sabotage Secretary-General Kofi Annan's attempt to reform the organisation. Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson presented an appeal signed by the 16 countries to Annan on Sunday during his visit to Sweden.

- Four Swedish companies have distributed new shares in spun off companies so far this year but information about the new share values sometimes do not reach shareholders until tax authorities send brochures, which is too late.

- Huge loans abroad and the slump in the Swedish crown at the beginning of the 1990s meant a large loss for the shipowner Sture Odner and his family company Odnia, which caused Nordbanken to cancel its loans to the company.
Odnia sued Nordbanken but has now lost in court and has to pay the bank another half a million crowns of court costs.

- Only 25 percent of all money invested in new listings on the Stockholm Stock Exchange has reached the companies themselves. The rest, or seven billion crowns, has ended up with previous shareholders.
Antonia Ax:son Johnson is the individual who has cashed in the most, one billion crowns, on bourse spin-offs.

- Broad funds in Sweden's largest fund group, Swedbank's Robur, have underperformed the Stocholm bourse's general index by one or two percentage points this year because they have not had enough shares in heavyweight telecoms group Ericsson .
- Construction shares will be hot this autumn but analysts warn that some of the companies might have a too narrow focus and that interest rates will not always remain as low as now.
